_about: NAVI defaults. Slider ranges are deliberately narrow so no setting can tip into AI slop. Values come from the W01 listening rounds; see reference/voice-rules.md. Every new review complaint should end up as a change here or a rule there.

eleven_v4.label: Eleven v4
eleven_v4.note: Sounds more natural. No speed setting, so pace comes from the script wording. Preferred over v3 overall in a blind comparison on 2026-11-05 (equal or better in every section); Alex is fully trained for it.

eleven_v3.label: Eleven v3
eleven_v3.note: For anyone who needs speed control: the Pace slider only applies to v3. Alex is not fully trained for it.

voice.rank_takes_by: finality of the last sentence (scripts/audio/finality.py), or pace closest to reference_pace_wps when set; then the ear. measure_speech.py flags problems but must not pick takes: it disagreed with the listener's ear on 4 of 7 experiments
voice.reference_take: output/test-todo-v4 (examples/test-todo-b.json, eleven_v4, Alex, the approved test voice)

casual.label: Casualness
casual.drives: script writing: contractions, 'gonna', 'kind of', run-on casual lines

energy.label: Energy
energy.drives: stability within the window (higher energy = lower stability) and word choice; tag stays [relaxed]

pace.label: Pace
pace.unit: ElevenLabs speed x 100 (eleven_v3 only; eleven_v4 has no speed setting)

hes.label: Hesitations
hes.drives: fillers and restarts per section written into the talking script; restarts never more than one per section
hes.high: Human, but too many sounds nervous

breath.label: Breaths
breath.drives: how much of the model's own breathing survives the edit; never adds breaths

swear.label: Swearing
swear.drives: light swears only at a slip or a surprise, or emphasis aimed at the product; never inside an instruction, number or warning, never at the viewer
swear.high: Only at a slip or a surprise, never in instructions

caps.2: at most one per 2 minutes, never more than 2 in a video

voices._note: Only Alex has been through listening rounds. Untested voices start from these guesses and must be judged by ear before being marked recommended.

on_screen.caption_look_note: Mona Sans on slightly rounded boxes by default. Helvetica Neue on square boxes stays as an option
on_screen.extra_overlays: never, unless the user adds them

recording.viewport_note: browser size; the video is always 1920x1080. 1440x810 makes a narrow app about a third bigger
recording.capture_scale_note: the browser's frames are 2x (2880x1620), so the 1080p video is sharp and a Recordly zoom (1.8x) still isn't blown up. 3x drops the capture to ~25 frames a second

casual.label: Casual style
casual.cursor: Recordly's cursor exactly, drawn by Recordly's own renderer with its fresh-install defaults (tahoe, size 2.5, sway 0.4, hides after 2 s idle, dips on click)

recordly.label: Recordly style
recordly.zooms: what Recordly's auto-zoom button adds (buildInteractionZoomSuggestions), depth 3

recording.cursor: Recordly's tahoe cursor in both styles, with the page's real cursor shape (arrow, I-beam, hand)
recording.click_feedback: none: no ring or ripple; the cursor dips briefly (Recordly's click)
recording.polish: recorder/polish: Recordly's own export renderer (2.0.0-beta.1, commit b2b2f2b, pinned in recorder/polish/recordly/PINNED.json). Recordly's files are never edited
recording.passes_note: one live take: the recorder's cursor arrives on each word by itself (landAt). A second take only when the first fails the join check (an action over 0.5 s from its word)
recording.hide_on_page_note: Page parts taken off the page (hidden, not blurred) before every take, the live page check and rehearsal: a site's own nag banner that is never part of a lesson. The largest element around the text that still holds little else. For example Whop's yellow 'Confirm your tax details' banner.

export.folder_note: the user can name any folder (their own project folder); never inside the skill's repo
export.file_names: named after the demo title: <title>.mp4, <title>.srt, <title> transcript.txt, <title> (720p preview).mp4

speed_copy.note: off by default; when on, export both the normal file and a sped-up copy (e.g. 1.35x for a course). The voice keeps its natural pitch (ffmpeg atempo)

script.first_mention: name plus where it is or what it looks like; after that the bare name

provisional._note: Starting values from our own coding of 18 demos (one coder, small sample); not yet judged by ear. See voice-rules.md section 1.

examples.saas: at most 1 per video under 5 min, personal only from the brief

privacy._about: reference/privacy.md. The three tiers and the patterns live in scripts/privacy/patterns.json. A demo picks a preset and can show or blur single categories ('privacy': {'preset', 'show', 'blur', 'hide_words'} in its script). Tier 1 can never be shown.

strict.label: Strict
strict.about: blur all personal info, usage, prices and dates too

test_account.label: Test account
test_account.about: fake data, so names and emails show; money, customers and counts stay blurred

privacy.blur_px_note: CSS pixels of blur on matched text and elements (24 real pixels at 2x). Apple's text recognition reads none of it
privacy.frame_scan: every distinct browser frame, read with Apple's built-in text recognition (Vision); anything readable that matches is blurred over its time and listed

app._about: The local app's engine side (Phase 7): scripts/app/ and scripts/batch/. Settings, saved logins and the data live in ~/Library/Application Support/NAVI; the key in the Keychain.

batch.credit_margin_note: a video is never part-generated: if finishing it would leave fewer credits than this, it's skipped with that reason
batch.credit_limit_note: the most a batch may spend without asking (Settings: batch spending limit); over it, the Go screen asks first
batch.quiet_note: live recording drifts on a busy Mac: before each recording the batch waits (up to quiet_wait_min minutes) until the 1-minute load average is under quiet_load, then records anyway and says so in the report
batch.parallel_note: the render of one video always runs while the next is voiced and timed. render_while_recording (also while the next is being recorded live) and record_parallel (2 or 3 live takes at once) are switched on only when scripts/focus/load_check.py shows a live take comes out the same that way on this Mac; a video that creates things in a test business is always recorded alone
batch.heavy_note: before each batch the user is told to quit any app using more than heavy_cpu % of a core (and any named in heavy_apps, empty by default); the Go screen shows the Mac's load (a busy Mac makes takes land late and renders slow)

jobs._about: Per-job models. Each job runs as its own headless Claude Code subagent (scripts/jobs/jobs.py) on the model and effort named here. Full model IDs only, never an alias. If a model is unavailable the next one in 'fallback' runs and the batch report says so. Every run is logged in the batch report with its model, effort, time and tokens.

blind_test.note: while on, every real batch's outline is planned once per arm; the plans are shown unlabelled (A/B/C, shuffled) and the user picks one before anything is explored or written

for the first 2 videos of a real batch (2 keeps the extra credits small): one draft per arm (same style of the day, same facts), each voiced once, shown as A/B/C shuffled with the arm hidden; the user's pick is recorded ($NAVI_DATA/blind-picks.jsonl) and the picked take is the one that ships. An arm whose model is unavailable is left out, never swapped for another model. 13 Nov 2026: claude-opus-4-6 dropped (19 min a draft, too slow for production); only claude-opus-5-5 medium against low. 13 Nov 2026, test lessons 1 and 2: claude-opus-5-5 medium won both picks (2 of 2) and is locked in as the writing model; the writing test is off. Turn it back on (enabled: true) to compare again

jobs.headless_note: a run nobody is watching (a batch) never falls back to Fable, whatever a fallback list says; a job whose own model is Fable (planning) still uses it

warn_after.why: the cut-off date set for this model

explore.note: what was explored on a site (per login and view) is kept in $NAVI_DATA/sites and given to the next video's explorer for this many days, so it only walks what is new (scripts/explore/memory.py)
